correctness.rationale: The object is exactly the union of sixteen combinatorially specified radius-one closed-neighborhood facets. An exhaustive 809-face computation checks all 2,752 cover incidences and the acyclicity of the 375 ordinary discrete-Morse pairs. The sole critical 1-cell and 56 critical 2-cells have an exact signed incidence row with 44 zeros and twelve entries ±2 (six each), computed separately by gradient recursion and integral unit-pivot cancellation. One degree-two 2-cell gives RP^2; the other 55 attach nullhomotopically, establishing the full claimed homotopy type. Independent mod-2 and mod-3 boundary ranks on the original complex match the resulting homology. No infinite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The Clebsch graph is the canonical five-dimensional folded cube and a distinguished strongly regular graph. Unlike every ordinary hypercube at scale two (known to yield only two-sphere wedges), its closed-ball Čech nerve has an explicit projective-plane summand and integral two-torsion. The exact homotopy classification (not only finite-field homology), its 55-sphere multiplicity and non-shellability supply a natural structural boundary example for graph metric thickenings. The finite and precise nature of the fact is directly motivated by antipodal folding, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
